title: Explicit small inner-horn completion and universal restriction lifting
statement:
Fix Grothendieck universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal V$, with simplicial sets, horns, quasicategories and internal functor simplicial sets as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. For a $\mathcal U$-small simplicial set $X$, put $X_0=X$. Define $X_{r+1}$, for $r\in\mathbf N$, by attaching one $\Delta^n$ along each simplicial map $a:\Lambda_i^n\to X_r$, for every $n\geq2$ and $0<i<n$: explicitly
$$X_{r+1}=X_r\amalg_{\coprod_{(n,i,a)}\Lambda_i^n}\coprod_{(n,i,a)}\Delta^n.$$
Set $RX=\operatorname{colim}_{r<\omega}X_r$, with the pushouts and colimit computed degreewise in sets, and let $j_X:X\to RX$ be the inclusion. Then $RX$ is a $\mathcal U$-small quasicategory and $j_X$ is a degreewise monomorphism and an inner-horn cell map. Here an inner-horn cell map is a countable composite of pushouts of small coproducts of the indicated inner horn inclusions. It is inner anodyne in the lifting sense of [lem-coef-inner-anodyne-pushout-product], even when tested against inner fibrations in $\mathcal V$. For every $\mathcal V$-small quasicategory $E$, the actual restriction map
$$j_X^*:\operatorname{Fun}(RX,E)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Fun}(X,E)$$
is a map between quasicategories with the right lifting property against every degreewise monomorphism of $\mathcal V$-small simplicial sets: every commutative square with such a left map has a diagonal making both triangles commute. The inclusions $j_X$ and the maps $R(f)$ induced by relabelling each attached simplex $(n,i,a)$ by $(n,i,f_ra)$ are functorial in simplicial maps $f:X\to Y$. These same objects, maps and lifting assertions remain valid in any further containing universe. The empty simplicial set is sent to itself.

source.place: Small-object inner-anodyne replacement used in the proof of Corollary 2.2.5.4 (printed p.92, PDF p.109), and Corollaries 2.3.2.4-2.3.2.5 (printed pp.100-101, PDF pp.117-118). The explicit countable construction, same-universe size bound and stability against larger test objects are the agent formulation of this construction. Read online 2026-10-17; WANTED: archived HTT. No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical theorem.

proof.text:
Construct the displayed pushout in each degree as the quotient of the disjoint union of $(X_r)_m$ and the sets $(\Delta^n)_m$ labelled by $(n,i,a)$, identifying each horn simplex with its image under $a$. Because every horn inclusion is injective, this quotient has the set presentation
$$ (X_{r+1})_m=(X_r)_m\amalg\coprod_{(n,i,a)}((\Delta^n)_m\setminus(\Lambda_i^n)_m). $$
This is a presentation of sets; the simplicial operators on a new simplex use its attached simplex and, if its restriction lies in the horn, the attaching map. The quotient relations are preserved by every simplicial operator, so these operators are well-defined and satisfy the simplicial identities. In particular $X_r\to X_{r+1}$ is injective in each degree. Each set of attaching maps is a subset of $\prod_{m\geq0}\operatorname{Set}((\Lambda_i^n)_m,(X_r)_m)$; it and the countable union over $(n,i)$ belong to $\mathcal U$. Closure of a Grothendieck universe under these products, disjoint unions and quotients proves by induction that every $X_r$ is $\mathcal U$-small. The countable degreewise union is $RX$, is $\mathcal U$-small, and contains $X$ degreewise injectively. Its filtration is exactly the required countable inner-horn cell presentation.

source.place: Proposition 4.1.3.2, degreewise pushout construction, specialized to the map to a point; explicit quotient and universe check by the agent.

proof.text: Every map $b:\Lambda_i^n\to RX$ factors through a finite stage. Indeed the horn is the union of the finitely many $(n-1)$-faces $d_k\Delta^{n-1}$ for $k\ne i$, by [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Choose a stage containing the image under $b$ of the top simplex of each such face, and take the maximum of these finitely many stages. All their restrictions then lie in this same $X_r$. On overlaps the restricted maps agree in $X_r$, since they agree in $RX$ and $X_r\to RX$ is injective. Thus they give $a:\Lambda_i^n\to X_r$ with composite $b$. The simplex labelled $(n,i,a)$ in $X_{r+1}$ fills $b$ in $RX$. This works for every $n\geq2$ and $0<i<n$, proving that $RX$ is a quasicategory. The finite-stage argument uses the displayed finite face cover, not a claim that the horn has finitely many simplices in all degrees.

source.place: Proposition 4.1.3.2, final finite-horn factorization argument, and Corollary 4.1.3.3; the face-cover argument expands finiteness directly.

proof.text: For $f:X\to Y$, set $f_0=f$. Given $f_r$, send the old summand $X_r$ by $f_r$ followed by $Y_r\to Y_{r+1}$, and send the attached copy of $\Delta^n$ labelled $(n,i,a)$ identically onto the attached copy labelled $(n,i,f_ra)$. On that copy's horn the two prescriptions agree, so they descend through the pushout to $f_{r+1}$. The stage maps commute with the inclusions and hence induce $R(f)$ on the union. The identity relabels every cell by the same label. For $g:Y\to Z$, the two successive relabellings send $(n,i,a)$ to $(n,i,g_rf_ra)$, exactly the relabelling for $gf$; induction on $r$ proves equality on old summands too. Thus $R(1)=1$ and $R(gf)=R(g)R(f)$, and $R(f)j_X=j_Yf$.

source.place: Proposition 4.1.3.2, functoriality of simultaneous attachment; explicit identity and composition check.

proof.text: Fix any containing universe $\mathcal W$ large enough for the test simplicial sets. The filtration of step 1 is also a $\mathcal W$-small continuous transfinite composite (of shape $\omega$) of pushouts of small coproducts of inner horn inclusions. Apply [lem-coef-inner-horn-cell-generation] in $\mathcal W$. This cell map is a retract of itself, so the equality of classes in that node puts $j_X$ in the class of maps having the left lifting property against every $\mathcal W$-small inner fibration. This proves the asserted lifting meaning of inner anodyne, including the case $\mathcal W=\mathcal V$. In particular for a quasicategory $E$ in that universe, the map $E\to\Delta^0$ is an inner fibration by the horn definition in [lem-coef-inner-anodyne-pushout-product], and every inner anodyne map extends into $E$.

source.place: Lines 43 and 89-92, instantiated in the universe of the test objects; the same cell presentation is used, rather than a new small-object replacement.

proof.text:
We will use the actual exponential correspondence for the internal functor objects of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. A map $t:P\to\operatorname{Fun}(K,E)$ gives $\widehat t:K\times P\to E$ by
$$\widehat t_m(k,p)=t_m(p)_m(k,\operatorname{id}_{[m]}).$$
Conversely, from $v:K\times P\to E$ define $t_m(p):K\times\Delta^m\to E$ by sending an $s$-simplex $(k,\theta:[s]\to[m])$ to $v_s(k,P(\theta)p)$. Naturality in every monotone map shows that both formulas are simplicial. Substituting one into the other returns $v$ on each $(k,p)$; in the other direction naturality of $t$ returns the value of $t_m(p)$ on every $(k,\theta)$. Hence the formulas are inverse, and commute exactly with restriction in $K$, precomposition in $P$ and postcomposition in $E$. They apply to arbitrary simplicial sets $P,K$, not only simplices or quasicategories.

source.place: Degreewise expansion of the internal-Hom adjunction used in Proposition 1.5.7.6; both inverse formulas are checked directly from the definition.

proof.text: Let $K$ be any simplicial set in the test universe and $E$ a quasicategory there. A horn $\Lambda_i^n\to\operatorname{Fun}(K,E)$ corresponds by step 5 to $K\times\Lambda_i^n\to E$. The inclusion $h:\Lambda_i^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ is inner anodyne: every lifting problem against an inner fibration is precisely one of its defining horn problems. Apply [lem-coef-inner-anodyne-pushout-product] with $i=h$ and $j:\varnothing\hookrightarrow K$. Its pushout-product is $\Lambda_i^n\times K\to\Delta^n\times K$; permuting factors gives $K\times\Lambda_i^n\to K\times\Delta^n$. The extension into $E$ exists since $E\to\Delta^0$ is an inner fibration. Its adjoint is a filler for the original horn. Consequently $\operatorname{Fun}(K,E)$ is a quasicategory; take $K=X$ and $K=RX$.

source.place: Theorem 1.5.3.7 via the pushout-product argument of Lemma 1.5.7.5 / HTT Corollary 2.3.2.4; no additional functor-category closure theorem is assumed.

proof.text:
Consider a commutative square with left side a degreewise monomorphism $u:P\hookrightarrow Q$ and right side the actual restriction $j_X^*$. By step 5, its top and bottom maps are respectively maps
$$RX\times P\to E,\qquad X\times Q\to E,$$
whose restrictions agree on $X\times P$. Thus they define a single map from
$$T=(X\times Q)\amalg_{X\times P}(RX\times P)$$
to $E$. Step 4 and [lem-coef-inner-anodyne-pushout-product], applied in the universe containing $P,Q,E$, say that $T\to RX\times Q$ is inner anodyne. Since $E\to\Delta^0$ is an inner fibration, the map $T\to E$ extends to $RX\times Q\to E$. Its adjoint $Q\to\operatorname{Fun}(RX,E)$ is a diagonal in the original square. Restriction to $RX\times P$ recovers the top map, and restriction to $X\times Q$ recovers the bottom map, so both triangles commute as actual simplicial maps.

source.place: Proposition 1.5.7.6; all-monomorphism lifting proved by the displayed pushout-product, retaining strict triangles.

proof.text: The size and lifting assertions are stable under further enlargement: maps between two fixed $\mathcal U$-small simplicial sets form a subset of a $\mathcal U$-small product of function sets. Passing to a larger universe adds no functions between these fixed sets and therefore no labels $(n,i,a)$. Using the degreewise quotient presentation of step 1 at each stage and the union at the limit gives the same objects and the same relabelling maps. Step 4 applies the existing cell-generation theorem in each chosen test universe, and steps 6-7 apply the pushout-product theorem there, so arbitrary larger test objects are covered without asserting that inner anodyne lifting in the smaller universe alone implies lifting in the larger one. Finally every inner horn with $n\geq2$ is nonempty (it contains vertices); hence no map from it to $\varnothing$ exists. Starting from $X=\varnothing$ there are no attachments at any stage and $R\varnothing=\varnothing$. The resulting restriction is the identity on $\operatorname{Fun}(\varnothing,E)=\Delta^0$, consistent with all preceding assertions.

source.place: Agent universe-absoluteness and empty-case verification for the explicit construction of Proposition 4.1.3.2; the lifting theorems are reapplied in each containing universe.
